On April 21, Roewe held a grand launch event for its 20th anniversary and the new AI series product, themed "The First." Roewe, in collaboration with Volcengine, officially unveiled the world's first AI-native automotive series, "Jiayue," and introduced the industry's first AI-native technology architecture, "CPP." The first concept car of the Jiayue series, the Jiayue 07, made a stunning debut, ushering in a new era of AI-native vehicles with groundbreaking technological capabilities, delivering a transformative smart mobility experience for Chinese families.  

Roewe and Volcengine have deepened their partnership to drive the transition from "automotive + AI" to "AI-native vehicles." As the cloud and AI service platform under ByteDance, Volcengine's Doubao large model handles over 120 trillion tokens daily, ranking among the global top tier. Unlike the industry's common "AI in the car" approach, Roewe and Volcengine are exploring a more profound AI automotive path: through joint definition of interaction experiences and collaborative development of AI platforms, they achieve a more proactive, deeper, and integrated cooperation model. From the initial design phase of AI automotive products, the two sides established a joint R&D project team, adhering to the core concept of "AI go first," and deeply collaborated in areas such as AI-native technology architecture, intelligent cockpits, and vehicle-cloud integration to build a shared technology foundation.  

Focusing on the construction of AI-native vehicles, Roewe has comprehensively innovated from underlying capabilities and core technologies to overall architecture, deeply integrating the AI capabilities of Volcengine's Doubao large model. This marks the first time an AI large model has been deeply embedded into a physical vehicle, enabling the scheduling, decision-making, and execution of physical devices, achieving a leap from AI as a mere "interactive tool" to a core driver of the vehicle.

El primer concepto de la serie Jiayue, el Jiayue 07, hizo una impactante aparición, inaugurando una nueva era de automóviles nativos de IA con una capacidad tecnológica revolucionaria, ofreciendo a las familias chinas una experiencia de movilidad inteligente trascendental. La profunda cooperación entre Roewe y Volcano Engine impulsa la transición del automóvil de "automóvil + IA" a "automóvil nativo de IA". Como plataforma de servicios de nube e IA bajo ByteDance, el modelo Doubao de Volcano Engine tiene un volumen diario de llamadas de tokens.

Across four sessions, over a dozen top R&D and planning experts took turns explaining the AI evolution from a single grain of rice to the entire home. This was no ordinary technology briefing, but rather a deep narrative centered on "how innovation happens." A line from the "Outline for Building a Strong Intellectual Property Country" recently issued by the State Council was repeatedly cited: "Intellectual property not only protects outcomes but also organizes innovation." This statement fits Midea perfectly. While the industry was still debating whether "smart homes are a false proposition," Midea had quietly accomplished two major feats: embedding AI into over 150 categories of small appliances and building a "patent Great Wall" of over 165,000 patent applications worldwide. Yet, more intriguing than the data are the hidden details. A R&D engineer with a decade of experience in rice cooking revealed that, to ensure "perfect rice no matter how much water you add," they spent nearly 16 years since 2010 mapping the industry's first Chinese rice map. A microwave expert disclosed that a single AI vision cooking system alone has over a hundred invention patents. Meanwhile, the head of whole-home smart products bluntly stated, "The industry is all about connecting large models, but only we truly understand home appliances." This is no longer the Midea you remember as merely "making air conditioners and selling rice cookers." From the "home brain" to the "factory brain," from human-vehicle-home connectivity to humanoid robots, Midea is now driven by the dual engines of AI and patents.

Background  
Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models are becoming the core architecture for robotic intelligence, but existing mainstream approaches (e.g., OpenVLA, π0, CogACT) suffer from a fundamental flaw: using a single action model to handle all types of actions uniformly. This "one-size-fits-all" design exposes two inherent contradictions in robotic manipulation tasks.  

From the perspective of task characteristics, robotic manipulation involves two essentially different types of actions: large arm movements (coarse actions) require global scene understanding with loose path constraints, while fine gripper operations (fine actions) demand local precision, accurate grasping poses, and extremely low error tolerance. These two action types differ fundamentally in path constraints, visual attention, and data distribution, making it inherently conflicting for a single model to balance "coarse positioning" and "fine manipulation."  

Furthermore, traditional methods lack active perception and routing mechanisms for action types, failing to dynamically allocate appropriate reasoning resources based on the current manipulation stage. This leads to a rapid accumulation of errors as steps increase in long-horizon complex tasks. DAM-VLA (Dynamic Action Model-Based Vision-Language-Action) is the first to decouple arm movement and gripper operation modeling, incorporating a dual-scale weighting mechanism to achieve precise and efficient robotic manipulation.

More importantly, AI is transitioning from a "capability competition" to "system deployment"—how to operate stably, evolve continuously, and truly embed into human society and industrial systems in the real world. A new generation of system paradigms, represented by agents, is emerging. AI is no longer just a tool for generating content but is gradually integrating into workflows, with capabilities for continuous perception, decision-making, and execution. From "answering questions" to "completing tasks," from single-turn interactions to long-sequence closed loops, AI is evolving into a system form that participates in actions and decisions. Meanwhile, world models oriented toward the physical world are accelerating development. From multimodal understanding to spatial and dynamic modeling, AI is beginning to depict the evolution laws and causal mechanisms of the real world with "states" as the core, moving from "generating symbols" to "interacting with the physical world." Agents require stronger world modeling capabilities to execute stably in complex environments, while world models need actions and feedback to form closed-loop learning and continuous optimization. Thus, AI development enters a new phase—"intelligent systems" capable of operating in the real world. However, alongside capability leaps, a series of critical issues are becoming increasingly prominent, including how to construct next-generation AI technology pathways and future system forms, how to embed alignment and governance upfront rather than as post-hoc fixes, and how to achieve intelligent business closed loops. The 8th Beijing Zhiyuan Conference will address these topics.
excerpt_i18n.es: Este año, la lógica subyacente del desarrollo de la inteligencia artificial está cambiando. El entusiasmo no se ha desvanecido, sino que se acelera. Un cambio aún más importante es que la IA está pasando de una "competencia de capacidades" a una "implementación sistémica": cómo operar de manera estable en el mundo real, evolucionar continuamente e integrarse verdaderamente en la sociedad humana y los sistemas industriales. Está surgiendo un nuevo paradigma sistémico representado por los agentes inteligentes. La IA ya no es solo una herramienta para generar contenido, sino que se integra gradualmente en los flujos de trabajo, con capacidades de percepción continua, toma de decisiones y ejecución. Desde "responder preguntas" hasta "completar tareas", desde interacciones únicas hasta ciclos cerrados de largo plazo, la inteligencia artificial avanza hacia una forma sistémica que participa en acciones y decisiones.
